1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; AI: artificial intelligence; MDM: mobile device management; CI: continuous integration

  • How to configure Claude Code for a team: scopes, shared settings, managed policy
  • Team standards: CLAUDE.md, permissions, hooks, Skills, plugins, MCP
  • AI-assisted workflows and their guardrails
  • Operational enablement: debugging, incidents, cost and usage visibility

2Configuring Claude Code for Teams

Running case

Lumen Advisory Rolls Out Claude Code to a Bank's 300 Engineers

  • The bank's security team wants model and permission limits and no secrets exposure
  • Platform engineering wants shared standards and usage visibility by team
  • Developers want autonomy in their own folders

Four settings scopes

Scope File Applies to Use for
User ~/.claude/settings.json One developer, all projects Personal preferences
Shared project .claude/settings.json (commit it) Everyone in the repository Team permissions, hooks, plugins, project environment variables
Project local .claude/settings.local.json (kept out of git) One developer, one project Personal overrides
Managed Deployed by the organization (managed-settings.json, MDM, or server-managed settings from the admin console) Everyone it is deployed to Security policy and compliance

  • Precedence (highest first): managed, command line, project local, shared project, user. A key set higher overrides the same key below it; lists such as permission rules merge across scopes.
  • Managed settings lock what developers cannot change: allowed and denied models (availableModels, deniedModels), permission policy, telemetry destination, and more. A few restrictive keys are honored from any scope.
  • Repository files cannot grant everything: for example bypassPermissions and telemetry exporters do not take effect from project settings, and committed allow rules wait for the developer to trust the folder.
  • Verify with /status (which sources loaded) and claude doctor (rejected entries).
Exam tip

To enforce a policy developers must not override, use managed settings. To share team conventions, commit .claude/settings.json and CLAUDE.md. Personal tweaks belong in user or local files.

3Team Standards and Extensions

Mechanism Purpose Notes
CLAUDE.md (committed) Persistent project instructions: conventions, commands, architecture notes Keep concise; it loads into context
Permission rules (allow, ask, deny) What Claude may run or read Deny secrets files (for example .env) and dangerous commands
Hooks Deterministic scripts at events (for example before a tool runs) Enforce rules prompts cannot guarantee: block, format, log
Skills Reusable procedures loaded on demand Share review checklists, migration procedures
Plugins Bundle skills, commands, hooks and MCP servers for distribution Record sources and versions
MCP servers (shared config) Connect issue trackers, docs, databases Apply least privilege and OAuth (Module 8)
Sandboxing Contain commands and file access Reduce blast radius
Headless mode (claude -p) Run in scripts and CI Use scoped permissions; --bare skips auto-discovery for reproducible scripted runs [Verify live]
  • Secrets: never in CLAUDE.md or committed settings; deny reads of secret files; use environment variables and a secrets manager.
  • Model and cost control: restrict available models by policy; use OpenTelemetry to see cost and tokens by team.
  • Telemetry is off until enabled; metrics include cost, token usage by type, sessions, commits, pull requests and tool decisions; prompt content is not logged by default; admins push settings through managed settings; add team and cost-center attributes with OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (watch label cardinality).
Exam tip

Managed settings enforce what developers must not override; committed CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json share conventions.

Exam tip

Hooks and permission rules enforce deterministically; a sentence in CLAUDE.md is only guidance.

4AI-Assisted Developer Workflows

Workflow How Claude helps Guardrail
Code understanding Explore a large codebase, explain modules Verify claims against the code
Implementation Plan, then implement changes across files Plan mode first; small reviewed diffs
Tests Generate and extend tests; run them Tests are the verification; review test quality
Code review First-pass review in CI against team rules Human reviewers remain accountable
Documentation Draft and update docs Review for accuracy
Migrations and refactors Repetitive edits at scale Scripted checks, staged rollout
  • Verification over trust: run tests, linters and type checks; require review; do not merge unreviewed AI changes.
  • Plan first for non-trivial work; keep changes small.
  • Capture lessons in CLAUDE.md and Skills so the next session starts better.
  • Measure productivity honestly (cycle time, review time, defect rate), not only lines produced.
  • Protect IP and data: control what code and data may leave the environment; use managed policy and approved platforms.

5Debugging and Operational Support

  • Incident triage: Claude can read logs, traces and recent changes, form hypotheses and propose fixes; keep read-only access by default and approval for production changes.
  • Reproduce first: use request ids, trace ids, prompt and model versions to replay (Module 12).
  • Runbooks as Skills: encode diagnosis procedures so responders and Claude follow the same steps.
  • Observability access: connect monitoring and ticket systems through MCP with least privilege.
  • Post-incident: update runbooks, evals and CLAUDE.md with the lesson.
  • Usage visibility: dashboards of cost and tokens by team, budgets and alerts; Claude Code analytics and usage APIs report per-user estimates for governance.

6Exam Q&A

S1A security team must ensure developers cannot use unapproved models or bypass permission policy. Which mechanism enforces this?

  • AManaged settings deployed by the organization, such as allowed and denied models and permission policy
  • BA shared project settings file that each developer can override locally for their own sessions at any time
  • CA reminder in the onboarding document
  • DA line in the committed CLAUDE.md asking developers to use only the approved models for all their work
Show the answer

Answer: A. Managed settings sit at the top of precedence and cannot be overridden.

S2Where should team conventions such as build commands and architecture notes be stored so every developer's sessions use them?

  • AIn the local settings file that is kept out of git and is private to each developer
  • BIn a committed CLAUDE.md and shared project settings
  • CIn individual chat histories
  • DIn each developer's user settings
Show the answer

Answer: B. Committed, shared files give everyone the same standards.

S3A developer sets model in project local settings; a managed setting restricts allowed models. What happens?

  • AClaude Code stops running
  • BThe local setting wins because it is more specific than the organization's managed restriction
  • CThe managed restriction wins because managed settings have the highest precedence
  • DBoth are merged and the developer chooses
Show the answer

Answer: C. Managed policy has the highest precedence, so a project-local value cannot override an organization's model restriction.

S4Which TWO enforce behavior deterministically rather than by instruction? Select TWO.

  • AA deny permission rule for commands that delete data
  • BA comment in the code
  • CA hook that blocks reading secret files before a tool runs
  • DA request in the pull request template
  • EA sentence in CLAUDE.md asking Claude to avoid risky commands
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Hooks and permission rules are enforced by the tool, not by the model's compliance.

S5The platform team wants cost and token usage by team from Claude Code. What should they do?

  • AAsk developers to email their usage figures to the platform team at the end of every single month
  • BEnable OpenTelemetry through managed settings and add team and cost-center resource attributes
  • CDisable telemetry to avoid privacy risk
  • DTurn on logging of all prompt text for every developer so that usage can be attributed to teams and cost centers
Show the answer

Answer: B. Telemetry through managed settings gives cost data; prompt content stays off by default.

S6A repository's committed settings try to configure the telemetry exporter and bypassPermissions. What is the result?

  • AThey are merged with managed settings
  • BThose keys do not take effect from repository files; policy should come from managed or user settings
  • CThey apply for everyone who clones the repository, as soon as each developer has trusted the project folder
  • DThey apply only on Mondays
Show the answer

Answer: B. Security-sensitive keys such as bypassPermissions and telemetry exporters are ignored from repository files and need managed or user settings.

S7An AI-generated change passes review quickly but later breaks production. Which workflow improvement is most relevant?

  • ARemove human review to move faster
  • BPlan first, keep diffs small, run tests and checks, and require meaningful human review
  • CMerge automatically after the model says it is confident, because its review is faster than a human's
  • DAsk Claude to review its own change only
Show the answer

Answer: B. Verification and accountable human review remain essential: plan first, keep diffs small, run tests and review meaningfully.

S8During an incident, an assistant should help diagnose a production fault. What access design is appropriate?

  • AFull production write access so that it can fix issues quickly without waiting for any approval
  • BNo access to any telemetry
  • CRead-only access to logs and traces by default, with human approval for production changes
  • DShared administrator credentials
Show the answer

Answer: C. Read-only access by default with approval for production changes follows least privilege during incident response.

S9A team wants a reusable diagnosis procedure that both responders and Claude follow. What fits best?

  • AAn email thread
  • BA larger model
  • CA paragraph pasted into every chat by each responder at the start of every incident they handle
  • DA shared Skill (runbook) loaded when the situation matches
Show the answer

Answer: D. A shared Skill packages the runbook as a procedure that loads when the situation matches, so responders and Claude follow the same steps.

S10Why is Claude Code telemetry not logging prompt text by default?

  • APrivacy by default: content logging is off unless explicitly enabled
  • BPrompt text cannot be logged technically
  • CTelemetry is not available in managed environments, where only the administrator can see usage
  • DIt would reduce the context window
Show the answer

Answer: A. Content gates are off by default and must be enabled deliberately.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Scopes User · shared project (commit) · project local (not committed) · managed (org)
Precedence Managed > command line > project local > shared project > user; lists merge
Policy Managed settings (models, permissions, telemetry); /status, claude doctor
Standards CLAUDE.md, permission rules, hooks, Skills, plugins, MCP, sandbox
Deterministic Hooks and permission rules, not prose
Telemetry Off until enabled; no prompt text by default; managed settings; team attributes
Workflows Plan, small diffs, tests, review, capture lessons
Ops Read-only by default; approval for prod changes; runbooks as Skills
